definitions.definition: IIR filter whose magnitude response decreases monotonically with frequency and approximates the ideal response as order increases; poles lie on a circle.
IIR filter whose magnitude response exhibits ripple in the passband or stopband; poles lie on an ellipse.
All-pole Chebyshev filter with equiripple behaviour in the passband and monotonic behaviour in the stopband.
Chebyshev filter with both poles and zeros, monotonic in the passband and equiripple in the stopband.
Recursive digital filter whose present output depends on present and past inputs and past outputs.
Realization where the present output is a function of past outputs, past and present inputs; corresponds to an IIR filter.
Realization where the present output depends only on past and present inputs; corresponds to an FIR filter.
IIR design method that digitizes an analog filter by sampling its impulse response.
One-to-one mapping from the s-plane to the z-plane that maps the left half-plane into the unit circle, avoiding aliasing.
Non-linear frequency compression at high frequencies introduced by the bilinear transformation.
Compensates warping by prescaling critical frequencies before applying the bilinear transformation.
Simplest analog-to-digital conversion approximating the derivative as (y(n)-y(n-1))/T.
Converts an analog filter to digital by mapping each s-plane zero/pole z to e^(sT).
IIR realization with separate delay chains for the numerator (zeros) and denominator (poles).
IIR realization sharing one delay chain, requiring max(M,N) memory locations.
Graphical representation of the relationships among variables of a set of linear difference equations.
Reversing branch directions and interchanging input/output leaves the system function unchanged.
Realization of a system as a product of lower-order sections to minimize quantization errors.
Realization obtained by partial-fraction expansion of H(z) into parallel first/second-order sections.
A causal and stable recursive filter cannot have phase response proportional to frequency because that would require poles outside the unit circle.
Non-recursive digital filter whose present output depends on the present and past inputs only; always stable.
System whose delay is constant across frequency, preserving signal shape; FIR can be exact if impulse response is symmetric.
Oscillations in passband and stopband caused by abrupt truncation of the infinite Fourier series.
Finite weighing sequence multiplied with the infinite impulse response to reduce Gibbs oscillations.
Adjustable window whose main-lobe width and side-lobe level can be varied via a parameter using a Bessel function.
FIR design technique that specifies the desired response at discrete points and obtains coefficients by IDFT.
An FIR filter is always stable because all its poles are at the origin.
Processing discrete-time signals at more than one sampling rate within a system.
Reducing the sampling rate by factor M by keeping every M-th sample and discarding the rest.
Increasing the sampling rate by factor L by inserting L-1 zeros between consecutive samples.
Filtering a signal with an anti-aliasing filter followed by downsampling to avoid aliasing.
Upsampling followed by filtering with an anti-imaging filter to remove image spectra.
Lowpass filter applied before downsampling with cutoff π/M to prevent aliasing.
Lowpass filter applied after upsampling with cutoff π/L to remove image spectra.
Converting a signal from one sampling rate to another by rational factor L/M using interpolation then decimation.
Spectral overlap that occurs when downsampling a signal not band-limited to π/M.
Extra spectral copies introduced by upsampling a discrete-time signal.
Sequence of quantities defined only at separate instants, obtainable by sampling a continuously varying waveform.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Series of samples satisfying x[n + N] = x[n] for every n, so the pattern repeats every N samples.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Sample pattern equal to one at index zero and zero at every other index, also called the Kronecker delta.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Discrete-domain processor obeying superposition whose behavior is unchanged by delaying the input, fully described by its impulse response.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Output h[n] produced when a unit sample at index zero is applied, completely characterizing a linear shift-invariant processor.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Output formula expressing a linear shift-invariant processor's response as the input combined with its characteristic output h[n].
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Property that the output at any instant depends only on present and past inputs, equivalent to an impulse response that is zero for n < 0.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Property guaranteeing finite outputs for every finite-amplitude excitation, which for discrete shift-invariant processors holds when the impulse response is absolutely summable.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Recurrence expressing each term of a sequence as a fixed-weight combination of earlier terms, used to describe discrete processors.
definitions.unitTitle: Introduction to Discrete-Time Signals and Systems

definitions.definition: Expansion of a repeating sample pattern into N complex exponentials that are harmonics of the fundamental digital frequency 1/N.
Transform mapping a sample sequence to a continuous function of angular frequency that repeats every 2π.
Transform mapping N complex numbers to N complex numbers, giving equally spaced samples of the DTFT of a finite sequence.
Transform recovering the original N samples using the opposite exponent sign and a 1/N normalization.
Duality where multiplying the input by a linear phase rotates the output indices modulo N, and a rotated input multiplies the output by a linear phase.
Operation combining two length-N sequences with indices wrapped modulo N, corresponding to pointwise multiplication of their DFTs.
Block-processing technique that splits a long input into segments, filters each using FFT-based circular operations after appended zeros, and sums the intersecting output pieces.
Block-processing technique that reuses the last M−1 input samples of each block, filters by circular operations, and discards the first M−1 corrupted outputs.
Brute-force computation straight from the defining sum of the transform, requiring N terms for each of N outputs, about N² operations.
Any algorithm computing the DFT or its inverse in O(N log N) operations, producing the same results as direct evaluation.
Divide-and-conquer scheme for power-of-two lengths that splits each transform into two half-length transforms, needing (N/2)log₂N complex multiplications.
Radix-2 splitting that separates the input into even-indexed and odd-indexed samples, transforms each half and combines the results.
Radix-2 variant, also known as the Sande–Tukey algorithm, obtained by reversing the order of the splitting steps of its time-domain counterpart.
Size-2 transform that combines even and odd sub-results by forming their sum and difference after scaling the odd part by a twiddle factor.
Complex root of unity that multiplies intermediate results between stages of a divide-and-conquer transform.
Permutation that swaps each index with the one whose binary digits are written in opposite order, restoring natural output order of in-place radix-2 algorithms.
Fast evaluation of x_n = (1/N)ΣX_k e^(i2πkn/N), obtained from a forward algorithm by flipping the exponent sign and scaling by 1/N.
Multicarrier modulation splitting data into parallel streams on closely spaced subcarriers whose mutual crosstalk is eliminated, generated by an inverse FFT at the transmitter.
